==English==

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=real|:inh|enm:really<ety:af<real><-ly<id:adverbial>>>|:afeq|real<id:actual>|-ly<id:adverbial>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|really}}, {{m|enm|realy}}, {{m|enm|rialliche}}, equivalent to {{af|en|real|-ly|id2=adverbial}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alter|en|real-ly|reälly}} {{q|both nonstandard}}

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪə.li/|[ˈɹʷɪə̯lɪ]|[-li]|[ˈɹʷɪː-]|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪl.i/|/ˈɹi.li/|/ˈɹi.ə.li/|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-really.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹiə.liː/|[ˈɹʷeə̯ɫiː]|[ˈɹʷiə̯-]|a=NZ}}
** {{homophone|en|rarely}}
* {{IPA|en|a=India|/ˈrɪ.jə.liː/|/rɪˈjɜː.liː/<a:emphasised>}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹeɪlɪ/|a=obsolete|ref={{R:Bingham IP|76}}}}
* {{hyphenation|en|re|al|ly||real|ly}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːli|s=2}}

====Adverb====
{{en-adv}}

# {{lb|en|literal}} In a way or manner that is [[real]], not [[unreal]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1751|author=John Roche|title=Moravian Heresy|page=168
|passage=We are to believe that by an ''extraordinary'' Conception by Means of the ''holy Ghost'' he in an ''extraordinary'' MANNER, (unknown to us) '''''really''''' assumed Flesh, and was by her nourished in the Womb and in due Time born in a natural Manner, and that whilst on Earth he was '''''really''''' hungry, and dry, and eat and drank as '''''really''''' as other Men, without, any Deception of Sight in us or Delusion whatsoever.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1878|author=Jonathan Baldwin Turner|title=Christ's Words as Related to Science,...|page=52
|passage=If we take the phenomenal world as it strikes our senses, in all its varied and wonderful powers and aspects; as the mere symbol of the Divine Presence and power, that is, according to Christ, ever in, through, and over all, as '''really''' as are causal light, heat and gravity, or as '''really''' as our own life and souls pervade every atom of our bodies, [...]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1975|author=Robin H. S. Boyd|title=An introduction to Indian Christian theology|page=48
|passage=Thus Brahman must be described as ‘'''really''' real’, while a rope, or a person, or God Himself, is ‘unreally real’. And it is only the Vedantin who can distinguish the real from the unreal, for to others all seems real.}}
# {{lb|en|modal}} Actually; in fact; in reality.
#: {{ux|en|"He '''really''' is a true friend."'' / ''"'''Really'''? What makes you so sure?"}}
# {{lb|en|informal|as an intensifier}} [[very|Very]] (modifying an adjective); [[very much]] (modifying a verb).
#: {{ux|en|But ma, I '''really, really''' want to go to the show!}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=10|passage=It was a joy to snatch some brief respite, and find himself in the rectory drawing–room. Listening here was as pleasant as talking; just to watch was pleasant. The young priests who lived here wore cassocks and birettas; their faces were fine and mild, yet '''really''' strong, like the rector's face; and in their intercourse with him and his wife they seemed to be brothers.}}
#* {{RQ:Christie Autobiography|II|4|passage=There was also hairdressing: hairdressing, too, '''really''' was hairdressing in those times — no running a comb through it and that was that. It was curled, frizzed, waved, put in curlers overnight, waved with hot tongs;{{nb...}}.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* Like its synonyms, [[really]] is, in practice, often used to preface an [[opinion]], rather than a [[fact]]. (See also usage notes for [[actually#Usage_notes|actually]].)
: ''Increasingly people are recognising what's '''really''' important is having children.''<ref name="The Sydney Morning Herald article prefacing opinoin with 'really'">{{cite-web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2005/01/14/1105582712427.html|title=The Sydney Morning Herald article 'When men turn clucky'|last=Marriner|first=C|date=15-01-2005|publisher=The Sydney Morning Herald|accessdate=2009-04-12}}</ref>

=====Alternative forms=====
* {{sense|in a way or manner that is real, not unreal}} {{l|en|real-ly}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|actually}} {{l|en|actually}}, {{l|en|in fact}}, {{l|en|indeed}}, {{l|en|truly}}; see also [[Thesaurus:actually]]
* {{sense|colloquial|as an intensifier}} {{l|en|so}}

====Interjection====
{{en-intj}}

# {{lb|en|informal}} {{n-g|Indicating [[surprise]] at, or requesting confirmation of, some new information; to express [[skepticism]].}}
#: A: ''He won the Nobel Prize yesterday.''
#: B: '''''Really?'''''
## {{lb|en|informal|by extension}} {{n-g|A [[phatic]] confirmation by a [[listener]], to signal [[active listening]]; mostly devoid of [[literal]] meaning, with the phatically [[contrived]] incredulity being merely formulaic.}}
##: A: ''You know, I saw Oliver the other day.''
##: B: '''''Really?''' What's he been up to?''
##* {{RQ:en:New York Times |date=1979-11-04 |author=William Safire |title=On Language [column] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1979/11/04/archives/on-language-the-fumblerules-of-grammar.html |passage="Literally" is not the only word that has lost touch with reality: look at "'''really'''." That word also was meant to describe a state of reality, or literalness. Even as a substitute for "Is that so?," the word asked, "Is that true, or real?" Nowadays, one guy goes, "I literally flew off the handle," and the other guy goes "'''Really'''." It's a grunt, meaning, "I'm still here."|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407133656/https://www.nytimes.com/1979/11/04/archives/on-language-the-fumblerules-of-grammar.html|archivedate=7 April 2023}}
# {{lb|en|informal|sarcastic, typically exaggerated question}} {{n-g|Indicating that what was just said was [[obvious]] and [[unnecessary]]; contrived [[incredulity]].}}
#: A: ''I've just been reading Shakespeare - he's one of the best authors like, ever!''
#: B: '''''Really?'''''
# {{lb|en|informal|chiefly|US}} {{n-g|Indicating affirmation, agreement.}}
#: A: ''That girl talks about herself way too much.''
#: B: '''''Really'''. She's a nightmare.''
# {{lb|en|informal}} {{n-g|Indicating [[displeasure]] at another person's [[behaviour]] or [[statement]].}}
#: {{ux|en|Well, '''really'''! How rude.}}

=====Usage notes=====
For the phatic sense, alternatives such as {{m|en|wow}} or {{m|en|gosh}} avoid a miscue whereby a speaker mistakes an active listener's ''really'' for genuine surprise or incredulity.

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|incredulity, phatically contrived incredulity, or in ironic/sarcastic sense}} {{l|en|gosh}}, {{l|en|is that so}}, {{l|en|no kidding}}, {{l|en|no really}}, {{l|en|no way}}, {{l|en|oh dear}}, {{l|en|oh my}}, {{l|en|oh really}}, {{l|en|you don't say}}, {{l|en|wow}}
* {{sense|affirmation, agreement}} {{l|en|actually}} {{q|Philippines}}
